newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros President grants islands more autonomy.
newsitem.headline: Comoros President grants islands more autonomy.

text.p: Comoros President Mohamed Taki has announced that the islands comprising the Indian ocean archipelago would be given more autonomy in a speech that disappointed secessionist leaders.

The islands would be divided into communes to grant each island more autonomy, said Taki, in a live address late on Friday on state television. The precise implications of the division remained unclear.
The speech did not mention a secessionist rebellion on Anjouan island.
Youths in the Anjouan capital Mutsamudu started rebuilding street barricades after the speech amid rumours of imminent military intervention to seize government buildings, witnesses said.

The Comoro Islands, with a population of 190,000, became independent from France in 1975. Residents of Anjouan, Comoros' second island, say independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and numerous coups, and want to return to French rule.

Three people including a gendarme were killed on July 14 as demonstrators who want Anjouan to return to French rule or become independent clashed with security forces. Several were also killed in March clashes.
France has denounced the pro-secessionists, saying the Anjouan situation is serious and could destabilise the whole region.
Taki promised to guarantee the independence of the judiciary. "Stability and credible justice remain the main elements which could attract investors," he said.
Opposition leader and former prime minister Mohammed Abdou Madi, was unimpressed by the speech, Radio Comoros reported.
"I am deeply shocked and confused by the fact that President Taki did not even mention once the Anjouan crisis," Madi was quoted as saying.

"I thought that Taki would come out with concrete and serious proposals which would re-establish trust in order to facilitate the search for a solution to the actual situation," said secessionist leader Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, 75, who was released from prison last week.
Speaking from his newly-renovated presidential residence Taki called on the population to remain confident in the authorities' ability to improve standards of living.
Taki denounced foreign and especially French media whom he accused of distorting and exaggerating events in the Comoros.
Talks between Taki and some secessionist leaders this week led to tension within the secessionist movement. Youths in Mutsamudu took down some barricades after the talks.
